title: feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule
body:
Stacked on #1163 (`issue/536-wire-taper` @ b14882ea, merged into this branch first). The wire base #1139, #1144, #1147 and #1160 are merged to main; #1150 and #1158 are pending. Merge order: #1163, then this PR. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A Wire Contour can now cut the ruled surface between two profiles given separately (#290 D2).

- **Op.** `WireContourOp.four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>` (`pairing`, `sync`, `tolerance`); absent by default, omitted from the file when absent, so a one-profile cut's file, stamp, CL and NC are unchanged. The pairing rule has no default in the file. Edited through `EditOperationParams` / the MCP parameter patch (the same JSON door); the page shows the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
- **Profiles.** The selection is read as two picks (a face's one outer ring, or a closed edge chain), each flat; the higher is the upper profile. Their heights must be the op's top and bottom planes (`app::operation::wire_ruled`).
- **Pairing** (`motion::wire_edm::pairing`). One monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors: by normalised arc length from each profile's point nearest the start hole, or by sync pairs with arc length between them. A ruling at every vertex of either ring; each move ends on a ruling's lower point, its pose the wire toward the upper point; upright at the start hole. The path's note states the rule.
- **Laws** (`motion::wire_edm::ruled_laws`). Fold: consecutive rulings whose ends run against each other (`a . b < 0` - the section turns back inside the part height). Crossing: the wire's section at a quarter height crosses itself. Ruled kerf: at 33 heights the wire's section stands off the stated surface by #1163's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)`.
- **A twisted ruled surface.** A straight wire cannot touch it along its whole height, so offsetting both profiles by the kerf gouges between the planes (about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf). The generator widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear at every height read, says in the notes how much stands on the profile planes, and refuses past the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm). A constant taper needs exactly #1163's `1 / cos(angle)`.
- **Refused by name:** crossed sync points ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"), doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points, a folding or self-crossing pairing, open profiles or one open and one closed, a ruling past `edm.max_taper_deg` (unstated refuses), a twist past the tolerance, profiles that are not two / not flat / not on the op's planes, a taper angle stated beside the two profiles, a lead whose leaning kerf enters the surface. The U/V stroke, U/V axes, guide planes and guide reach are #1163's machine check, unchanged (it reads poses).
- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's; kerf, threading and slug run at every judged height; a gouge blocks the post.
- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; `wire-iso.cps` writes the same `taper_on` / `uv` / `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes` as a tapered section and names the cut in a comment.

## Sources (Clean Room)

Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surface between two parametrised curves, chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", CAD 27(12), 1995. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`.

## Refresh (2026-11-13: #1163's refresh merged in, then upstream main @ a5d1a763)

- Kept both sides (also `operation/types/mod.rs` against main's `SinkerPass` export): #1163's burnout, open-run clearance and sinker fields sit beside `four_axis` in the op, DTO, job, page and every `WireContourOp` test literal.
- A 4-axis cut with a no-core burnout is refused by name (the burnout is cut vertical only), like #1163's taper + burnout refusal. Open profiles and a left/right side stay refused by the ruled generator.
- Verify still reads a 4-axis cut's poses as the wire's lean, and the leaning kerf is judged at every height. The new `burnout` flag is carried through.
- Main's posted-golden law asks a gate to judge every posted golden. `crates/app/tests/posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs` regenerates `wire_4axis_punch.cl` (byte-identical) and judges it with `taper: true` against the loft's own mesh, sliced at 25 heights: no finding, and the punch frees the part (`solid_law_goldens::the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates`). No law was loosened.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wire_4axis.rs`
  - `a_square_to_round_punch_posts_its_golden_and_verifies` - goldens `tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` (a pose on every move) and `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` (synthetic fixture); the wire clause reports no problem.
  - `a_constant_taper_by_sync_points_is_the_taper_golden_and_arc_length_differs` - the CL equals #1163's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte, the NC equals `wire_taper_punch.nc` but for the comment naming the cut; arc length on the same two profiles gives other rulings.
  - `crossed_folded_and_unpaired_sync_points_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pairing_past_the_machine_or_off_the_planes_is_refused_by_name` (max taper at generation, U stroke at the post, one profile, taper + 4-axis, planes off the profiles)
  - `a_ruling_that_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
  - `the_four_axis_block_round_trips_and_its_rule_is_never_defaulted` (JSON door, stamp, undo, the door's refusal of a NaN tolerance)
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_tests.rs` (8 tests): square-to-round keeps the kerf out and a zero tolerance refuses it; arc length vs sync points; the constant taper equals `wire_contour_tapered` move for move; crossed / folded / unpaired / off-profile / doubled sync points; open and mismatched profiles; steep rulings; a conical die.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/536-wire-taper` green on the final head 263442bc (motion lib, the whole app suite set - a new golden is shared test input - and the mapped ui suites; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture with invented codes.
- The die side at the app level (the motion crate pins a conical die); a die whose start hole is equidistant from several sides has no single nearest point - its arc-length seam is then the first tie, and a pairing that folds or twists for it is refused, not guessed.
- A model whose tessellated twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface of its two end profiles is refused by the wire laws as a gouge (the fixtures here are split along the inner diagonal). Follow-up #1170.
- Sync points are numbers on the page, not viewport picks (#1171). Fans and profiles stitched from several runs are refused by name (#1172). Open-profile 4-axis waits for #1109.
- UI: the new rows have no structural-test assertion of their own; no snapshot PNG was changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's DTO notes are not updated (a process file); the block rides `params` through the existing tools (#1108).

Changelog: Wire EDM 4-axis: a Wire Contour cuts the ruled surface between separately picked upper and lower profiles, paired by arc length or by sync points; crossed, folding or unpaired pairings, rulings past the machine's taper and U/V limits and a twist past the stated tolerance are refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #537

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Geometry tab of a Wire Contour on the wire EDM machine (Punch side, start hole stated).

**Before** (base `b3504f7e`): no 4-axis block.

![Wire Contour page, before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1181/before.png)

**After, pairing by arc length** (head `58f75a5f`): the 4-axis checkbox on, with the Pairing choice and Twist tolerance rows.

![Wire Contour page, after, arc-length pairing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1181/after-arclength.png)

**After, pairing by sync points** (head `58f75a5f`): two sync pairs stated, with their X/Y rows and the Remove / Add sync pair buttons.

![Wire Contour page, after, sync-point pairing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1181/after-sync.png)

Rendered headless: egui_kittest `Harness::render()` on lavapipe (software Vulkan), through the real `pages::properties` code, in a scratch test that is not in the branch.
